To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the frontal parietal control system is a key element of the neural network involved in internally driven thought and that (2) it is involved in the maintenance of internally generated thought, but not in the initiation of such thoughts.
(1) The default mode network is active when the mind wanders, and (2) the default mode network interacts with the frontal-parietal network during internally driven thought.
(1) the DMN is involved in internal cognition, and (2) the FPN is involved in external cognition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the brain generates and sustains a train of thought unrelated or only loosely related to the external world.
the neural correlates of the ability to produce and maintain a stream of internally generated thought.

how we can understand the neural basis of conscious experience, and we have focused in particular on the neural correlates of internally driven thought, and the way this thought is sustained and maintained in a state of perceptuo-motor decoupling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the default network is not the default mode network.

the DMN is a network of brain regions whose activity is correlated with the production and maintenance of internally guided thought, and which is associated with a state that has been termed “mind-wandering.”
The default mode network is a network of brain regions that is active when a person is not focused on a specific task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the default mode network (DMN) and the executive control network (ECN) are two distinct networks that have opposing functions.
it provides a novel framework for the study of the neural mechanisms of internally guided thought.
the default mode and task positive networks are not antagonistic, but rather, that they are complementary and cooperative.

we have shown that there are two types of attention: external attention and internal attention.
there are two main neural networks that support internal thought, and that these networks interact to support internal thought.
